title: Jerk Chicken & Peas and Rice
seoTitle: Jerk Chicken & Peas and Rice | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Charred jerk thighs, coconut rice and peas, island sides for eight
subtitle: Charred jerk thighs, coconut rice and peas, island sides for eight
description: A full Caribbean hall dinner — jerk-marinated chicken, coconut rice and peas, grilled pineapple, and sharp cabbage slaw. Sized for eight, with grill-or-oven paths and a call-interruption plan rookies can follow without opening another tab.
equipment: Grill with lid (or two sheet pans + oven)
Large hotel pans or sheet trays

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs
ingredients.notes: about 16–20 pieces; pat dry before marinating

ingredients.name: Scotch bonnet or habanero peppers
ingredients.notes: stemmed; seeds optional for less heat

ingredients.name: Full-fat coconut milk
ingredients.notes: 13.5 oz each; shake cans before opening

ingredients.name: Whole Scotch bonnet pepper
ingredients.notes: for rice pot only — do not pierce if you want milder rice

ingredients.name: Coleslaw mix or shredded green cabbage

steps.title: Trim and prep the chicken
steps.instruction: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels — wet skin will steam instead of char. Trim excess flap and hanging fat, but leave the skin on for color and juice. Score the skin lightly in two places per thigh so marinade penetrates. Lay thighs in two large zip bags or a hotel pan for marinating.

steps.title: Blend the jerk marinade
steps.instruction: In a blender, combine Scotch bonnets, green onions, thyme, garlic, ginger, allspice, brown sugar, soy sauce, lime juice, vegetable oil, 1 tbsp kosher salt, and black pepper. Blend until mostly smooth — a little texture is fine. Taste a tiny dab on a spoon: it should be salty, sweet, and sharply aromatic before it ever touches raw chicken.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.instruction: Massage marinade into every thigh, working it under the skin where you can. For same-day service, marinate at least 45 minutes in the fridge — flip once halfway. For best flavor, marinate 4–12 hours. Never leave raw chicken above 40°F; if the hall gets a call, back into the walk-in immediately.

steps.title: Set up grill or oven
steps.instruction: Grill path: preheat to 375°F with a two-zone fire — direct heat on one side, indirect on the other. Close the lid 10 minutes so grates are hot. Oven path: heat to 425°F and line two sheet pans with foil and wire racks. Oil the grates or racks so jerk sugars do not glue the chicken down.

steps.title: Start coconut rice and peas
steps.instruction: In a large pot, combine rinsed rice, kidney beans, coconut milk, chicken stock, sliced scallions, thyme sprigs, and the whole Scotch bonnet. Bring to a boil, stir once, then reduce to a low simmer and cover tightly. Cook 18–20 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice grains are tender — you want distinct grains, not mush. Remove thyme and pepper; fluff with a fork and hold covered at 200°F.

steps.title: Grill or roast the chicken
steps.instruction: Grill: place thighs skin-side down on direct heat 4–5 minutes until skin blisters and char lines appear, then flip and move to indirect heat with the lid down. Oven: roast skin-side up on racks 25–30 minutes. Either way, finish when the thickest part of the largest thigh reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer — juices run clear, not pink. If skin is pale, move pieces back to direct heat or under the broiler 2–3 minutes to crisp.

steps.title: Rest the chicken
steps.instruction: Transfer cooked thighs to a foil-lined sheet tray, tent loosely with foil, and rest 10 minutes. Carryover will push temp a few degrees past 165°F while juices redistribute. Do not slice yet — cut too early and the line gets dry chicken and a messy pan.

steps.title: Grill pineapple and dress slaw
steps.instruction: While chicken rests, grill pineapple rings over direct heat 2–3 minutes per side until caramelized grill marks show. Toss coleslaw mix with lime juice, a pinch of salt, and neutral oil — sharp and crunchy, not wet. Keep slaw cold on ice until the line opens.

steps.title: Coordinate timing for service
steps.instruction: Open the line when rice, chicken, and at least one hot side are ready — never hold rice more than 45 minutes dry in a hot box or it crusts on the bottom. Slice rested thighs into two pieces each for faster service. Put rice and peas in the first hotel pan, chicken in the second, pineapple and slaw in separate pans so textures stay distinct.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: close the grill lid or turn off the oven — chicken on indirect heat can hold safely up to 15 minutes. Turn rice to the lowest simmer or off and keep covered — do not stir or you release steam and dry the bottom. If tones drop after service, cover chicken and rice and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven; log hold time on the pan. On return, spot-check chicken at 165°F before reopening the line.

steps.title: Serve the hall line
steps.instruction: Set hot components closest to the crew: rice and peas first, then sliced jerk chicken with pan juices spooned over. Pineapple and cabbage slaw go at the far end; hot sauce and lime wedges in squeeze bowls between them. Tell the crew to hit the chicken with lime at the plate — acid wakes up the spice after a long shift.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool chicken and rice in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Refrigerate chicken and rice separately; slaw gets its own container. Reheat chicken to 165°F next shift; rice can be refreshed with a splash of water and covered heat. Sliced jerk chicken makes excellent next-day wraps with slaw and extra hot sauce.

proTips: Thighs beat breasts on the grill — more fat means more forgiveness if a rookie lingers on a call.
Shake coconut milk cans hard before opening; the cream separates and uneven pours make gluey rice.
Keep the whole pepper in the rice pot unpierced for milder crew heat; pierce it only if your hall runs hot.
Brush grates with oil right before chicken goes on — jerk sugar burns fast on dry metal.
Pull chicken at 163°F if you are holding under foil; carryover finishes the last degrees during rest.
If the grill flares from dripping marinade, move thighs to indirect heat — black smoke means bitter skin.
tonightSpread: Main: Jerk Chicken — charred bone-in thighs, sliced for the line with pan juices spooned over.
Sides: Coconut Rice and Peas, Grilled Pineapple rings, Sharp Cabbage Slaw (cold).
Condiments: Hot sauce, lime wedges, and extra jerk paste for crew who want more heat.
Set rice in the first pan, chicken in the second, cold slaw and pineapple at the far end so textures stay distinct.
Keep a backup tray of chicken at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.
leftovers: Cool chicken and rice in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat chicken to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Store slaw separately — it wilts if stacked on hot rice overnight.
Reheat rice covered with a splash of water or stock over medium-low, stirring once, until steaming throughout.
Slice cold jerk chicken thin for next-day wraps with slaw, hot sauce, and a squeeze of lime — faster reheat, less dry-out than whole thighs.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Island heat without a one-protein plate — jerk chicken, coconut rice and peas, and cooling slaw on one counter. A flagship hall classic that feels like a real Caribbean spread, not solo grilled chicken.
substitutions: Kidney beans ↔ canned pigeon peas for a more traditional rice-and-peas profile.
Bone-in thighs ↔ bone-in drumsticks (same cook time; verify 165°F at the joint).
Grill ↔ 425°F oven on wire racks if weather or station policy keeps you inside.
